diagnostic_evidence.quote: By applying the triangle inequality and the lifting theorem (see~\cite[Sect. 6]{beirao2017stability}), we can write

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds the full energy of w = b - Pi^nabla_kappa b by the H^{1/2}(boundary) seminorm of its trace. That is a harmonic-lifting bound and is false for functions with nonzero Laplacian: any H^1_0 function has zero boundary seminorm and positive energy. Here Delta w = Delta b - Delta(Pi b) is a generally nonzero polynomial of degree kappa-2, so the interior contribution is ignored. The claimed inequality |b|_1^2 <= gamma_sharp |Pi b|_1^2 with a shape-uniform constant is the key 'self-stabilization' property, and it is not established by the argument given.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove the equivalence correctly, for example with a VEM stability/inverse-estimate argument that uses Delta b in P_{kappa-2} and the moment unisolvence (norm equivalence on the finite-dimensional scaled space, with shape-uniform constants). This is a contained new lemma.
issues.overall_effect: The uniform equivalence of |b|_1 and |Pi b|_1 on bubbles is unsupported. The lower bound in the stability of a_h (coercivity, including the choice beta_sharp=0 used in the numerics) and the splitting stability both depend on it. Well-posedness and all error estimates therefore rest on an unproved estimate.
issues.title: Self-stabilization of bubbles: lifting bound applied to a non-harmonic function
issues.why_classification: The statement is plausibly true and the architecture survives, but a genuine new lemma with scaling and uniformity arguments is needed, which is more than a local fix.

issues.failure_explanation: The step |w|_{1,K} <= C |w|_{1/2,boundary K} is applied to w = v~ - Pi^nabla_k v~, where v~ lies in the enhanced space with Delta v~ in P_k. This w is not harmonic: Delta w = Delta v~ - Delta(Pi v~) is a generally nonzero polynomial. The bound therefore fails as an inference, since the interior part of the energy is not controlled by the trace. The subsequent scaling chain inherits the defect, so the lower bound eta(|v~|_1+|d|_1) <= |v_h|_1 is not established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the trace-theorem step by a correct estimate of |v~ - Pi_k v~|_1 for enhanced-space functions, using an inverse estimate for Delta v~ and the orthogonality constraints, as in the standard VEM stability analysis. This is a contained lemma.
issues.overall_effect: Uniform stability of the decomposition v_h = v~ + d_h is unproved. This is a stated structural property of the new element and is the tool needed to compare a(v~,v~)+a(d,d) with a(v_h,v_h).
issues.title: Splitting stability: trace/lifting step for a non-harmonic enhanced-space function
issues.why_classification: A known-type stability argument must be supplied for a separate proof step. The result and method survive, but the repair is more than routine.

issues.failure_explanation: Writing a(v~,v~)+a(d,d) = a(v_h,v_h) - 2a(v~,d), the correct remainder is -2C^star a(Q_k v~, d), with factor 2C^star, not -a(Q_k v~, d). In either form the term has no sign: a(Q_k v~, d) is generally nonzero and can be negative. The final inequality '<= C^star a(v_h,v_h)' simply drops it, so the upper bound is not proved. The cross term needs a Cauchy-Schwarz bound together with the splitting stability |v~|_1+|d|_1 <= C|v_h|_1, which is not invoked.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Bound a(v~,v~)+a(d,d) <= C a(v_h,v_h) using the splitting stability proposition (a short appeal to the already stated result), which gives the upper bound with a modified constant.
issues.overall_effect: Continuity of a_h, and hence continuity of B_h, rests on an unjustified inequality.
issues.title: Upper stability bound of a_h: cross term with no sign dropped
issues.why_classification: A short routine repair using an existing proposition fixes the step; the constants change but all claims survive.

issues.failure_explanation: By definition c_h only sees Q^0_k q_h = q_h - Pi^0_k q_h, so c_h(q_h,q_h) vanishes for every q_h that is elementwise a polynomial of degree <= k. Such nonzero q_h exist in Q_k (continuous piecewise polynomials with zero mean, or a global polynomial), so the lower bound by delta_star ||q_h||_0^2 is false. Only equivalence with sum_K ||Q^0_k q_h||^2 follows from the element estimate. The paper states that 'Thus, c_h satisfies' the full-norm equivalence, which does not follow from the element-wise estimate.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the two-sided bound with ||Q^0_k q_h||_{0,Omega} in place of ||q_h||_{0,Omega}, and check that the cited well-posedness argument uses only this form.
issues.overall_effect: The stated property is false, and any argument that uses it, such as the adapted proof of well-posedness, is unreliable. The later error analysis and the weak inf-sup proof use only the correct Q^0_k-version.
issues.title: False full-norm equivalence claimed for the pressure stabilization c_h
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction to the statement suffices, because the proofs that follow already use the corrected form.

For $v\in \mathrm{H}^{k+1}(\elementvem)$, the following optimal order error estimate holds true

issues.failure_explanation: The interpolant is defined (via nodal values) only for continuous functions, and the interpolation estimates require H^{k+1} regularity with rate h^{k+1}. In prop:added-6, v(q_h) is only in H^1_0(Omega), which has no nodal values in 2D. In cor:added-1, p is only in H^k, so for k=1 it is merely H^1. The dual pressure rho in thm:added-3 is only in H^1, yet ||rho-rho_I||_0 <= Ch||rho||_1 is used. None of these follows from the interpolation propositions as stated. A quasi-interpolation or best-approximation estimate in the conforming VEM spaces at low regularity is needed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Introduce a Scott-Zhang-type quasi-interpolant (or cite a low-regularity approximation result) for the enhanced spaces with the needed H^1 and L^2 estimates. Use it for v(q_h), p and rho, and rewrite the interpolation steps accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The weak inf-sup proof, the pressure part of the energy-error corollary at the stated regularity (p in H^k), and the dual-problem interpolation bounds in the L^2 velocity estimate are unsupported as written.
issues.title: Nodal interpolants applied to H^1 / low-regularity functions (velocity, pressure, dual pressure)
issues.why_classification: A contained new approximation lemma restores all statements with the same rates, but the repair is more than a local tweak.

issues.failure_explanation: The only proof of the discrete inf-sup/continuity result is a pointer to a theorem for a different (bubble-free equal-order) method with different b_h and stabilization. The paper's own ingredients are the weak inf-sup of prop:added-6, coercivity and continuity of a_h, and the properties of c_h. The argument combining them into a global inf-sup for B_h, with the right dependence of constants on alpha and the splitting of the test function, is never carried out. The result is unsupported as written.

failure_location.quote: The result is proved by adapting~\cite[Theorem 4.5]{guo2020new}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the standard Babuska-type argument: test with (u_h - theta v_p, p_h), where v_p comes from prop:added-6, choose theta small relative to alpha, and use coercivity and continuity of a_h and the bounds on c_h.
issues.overall_effect: Unique solvability of the discrete problem, the stability bound, and the quasi-optimality estimate that invokes 'the well-posedness' are not rigorously derived.
issues.title: Well-posedness of the discrete problem is asserted only by citation to a different element
issues.why_classification: The missing argument is a short, standard saddle-point computation built from results already stated; no new global machinery is needed.
